[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Gitflow Workflow: A Comprehensive Guide"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Gitflow is a branching model for Git, designed to manage releases and streamline parallel development. It provides a robust framework for larger projects, enabling teams to collaborate effectively and handle complex release cycles. This tutorial will guide you through the core concepts and practical implementation of the Gitflow workflow."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Branches"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Gitflow relies on two main branches with infinite lifetimes:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`main`: This branch reflects the production-ready state. All code on `main` is considered stable and deployable. It's also sometimes called `master`."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`develop`: This branch serves as the integration branch for features. All feature branches are merged into `develop`, and it reflects the next release."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Supporting Branches"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"In addition to the core branches, Gitflow uses several supporting branches with limited lifetimes:"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`feature` branches: These branches are used to develop new features. They branch off from `develop` and are merged back into `develop` when the feature is complete."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"# Create a new feature branch
git checkout -b feature/my-new-feature develop

# Finish the feature (merge into develop)
git checkout develop
git merge feature/my-new-feature
git branch -d feature/my-new-feature
git push origin develop"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`release` branches: These branches prepare for a new production release. They branch off from `develop` and allow for final tweaks and bug fixes before merging into both `main` and `develop`."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"# Create a release branch
git checkout -b release/1.2.0 develop

# Finish the release (merge into main and develop)
git checkout main
git merge release/1.2.0
git tag -a 1.2.0 -m "Release 1.2.0"
git checkout develop
git merge release/1.2.0
git branch -d release/1.2.0
git push origin main
git push origin develop
git push origin --tags"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`hotfix` branches: These branches are used to quickly patch production releases. They branch off from `main` and are merged back into both `main` and `develop` (or the current `release` branch)."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"# Create a hotfix branch
git checkout -b hotfix/1.2.1 main

# Finish the hotfix (merge into main and develop)
git checkout main
git merge hotfix/1.2.1
git tag -a 1.2.1 -m "Hotfix 1.2.1"
git checkout develop
git merge hotfix/1.2.1
git branch -d hotfix/1.2.1
git push origin main
git push origin develop
git push origin --tags"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Gitflow Workflow in Action"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"1. **Start a New Feature:** Create a new `feature` branch from `develop`."},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"2. **Develop the Feature:** Work on the feature, committing changes to the `feature` branch."},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"3. **Merge the Feature:** Once the feature is complete, merge the `feature` branch into `develop`."},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"4. **Prepare a Release:** When `develop` is ready for a release, create a `release` branch from `develop`."},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"5. **Finalize the Release:** Make any necessary final tweaks and bug fixes on the `release` branch. Merge the `release` branch into both `main` and `develop`. Tag the release on `main`."},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"6. **Hotfix Production Issues:** If a critical bug is found in production, create a `hotfix` branch from `main`. Fix the bug and merge the `hotfix` branch into both `main` and `develop` (or the current `release` branch). Tag the hotfix on `main`."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Gitflow Tools"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"Several tools can simplify the Gitflow workflow. One popular option is the `git-flow` extension. It provides commands to automate common Gitflow tasks."},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"# Install git-flow (example for macOS using Homebrew)
brew install git-flow

# Initialize git-flow in your repository
git flow init"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"After initializing, you can use commands like `git flow feature start <feature_name>`, `git flow feature finish <feature_name>`, `git flow release start <version>`, `git flow release finish <version>`, `git flow hotfix start <version>`, and `git flow hotfix finish <version>` to manage your branches."},{"order":26,"type":"subheading","text":"Advantages of Gitflow"},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Clear branching model for parallel development."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Simplified release management."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Easy hotfix implementation."},{"order":30,"type":"subheading","text":"Disadvantages of Gitflow"},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Can be overly complex for small projects."},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Requires strict adherence to the workflow."},{"order":33,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"Gitflow is a powerful branching model that can significantly improve the development process for larger projects. By understanding the core concepts and following the workflow, teams can collaborate more effectively and manage releases with greater ease. However, it's crucial to assess whether Gitflow is the right fit for your project's size and complexity before implementing it."}]
